goal_summary: Bounded source investigation and primary-literature curation of five uncurated IMA-approved single-reference critical-element mineral species from the September 2026 IMA-CNMNC Master List with open-access type descriptions in European Journal of Mineralogy (volumes 32, 36, 37, and 38): zhiqinite (IMA:2019-077), belmonteite (IMA:2024-040), dacostaite (IMA:2024-015), fluormacraeite (IMA:2024-054), and macraeite (IMA:2023-065). Reclassified bonacinaite (IMA:2018-056) to the multi-reference queue because the IMA Master List cites two references (Mineralogical Magazine 84 (2020), 568 and European Journal of Mineralogy 36 (2024), 863).

curated_sources_and_records.name: Zhiqinite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Inclusion in a corundum grain separated from podiform chromitite orebody Cr-11 (29°11' N, 92°18' E; elevation 5300 m), Kangjinla district, Luobusa ophiolite, ~200 km ESE of Lhasa, Tibet, China
type_specimens: Holotype M13817 (box of ~100 corundum grains containing TiSi2 inclusions) and FIB foil no. 4969 (used for 3D electron diffraction data collection), deposited at the Chinese Geological Museum, Xicheng District, Beijing 100034, China

primary_source.citation: Xiong F, Xu X, Mugnaioli E, Gemmi M, Wirth R, Grew ES, Robinson PT, Yang J (2020) Two new minerals, badengzhuite, TiP, and zhiqinite, TiSi2, from the Cr-11 chromitite orebody, Luobusa ophiolite, Tibet, China: is this evidence for super-reduced mantle-derived fluids? European Journal of Mineralogy 32:557-574

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: The Abstract (p. 557) reports the 3D ED unit cell of zhiqinite as a = 8.24(16) Å, b = 4.78(10) Å, c = 8.52(17) Å, V = 336(11) Å3, whereas Section 5.4 (p. 566) and Table 4 (p. 566) round the cell axes to a = 8.2(2) Å, b = 4.8(1) Å, c = 8.5(2) Å and Table 4 prints V = 335(11) Å3.

Table 3 (p. 564) prints the grain 302-4 average weight-percent sum (Si 52.89 + P 0.14 + Ti 43.25 + Cr 0.15 + Mn 0.28 + Fe 2.41 + Zr 0.44 + Ca 0.08 + Al 0.21) as 'Sum 100.00', whereas the arithmetic sum of the 9 printed mean values is 99.85 wt% (and the grain 302-4 average atomic-percent values sum to 99.83 at.% vs printed '100.00'). Similarly, in grain 409-3, point 1 wt% values sum to 100.02 wt% (at.% sum 100.01), point 4 wt% values sum to 100.01 wt% (at.% sum 100.02), and the grain 409-3 average wt% values (Si 55.26 + P 0.02 + Ti 44.33 + Cr 0.17 + Fe 0.23) sum to 100.01 wt% (at.% sum 100.01) vs printed '100.00'.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Belmonteite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Uppermost level (Level 250 m above sea level) of the dumps of the Cerille mine, fraction of Càstagnola, municipality of Framura, La Spezia province, Liguria, Italy
type_specimens: Holotype 20080 (Museo di Storia Naturale, Università di Pisa, Via Roma 79, Calci, Pisa, Italy)
Cotype MSNB 14957 (Museo Civico di Scienze Naturali 'E. Caffi', Piazza Cittadella 10, Bergamo, Italy)

primary_source.citation: Biagioni C, Bosi F, Bonaccorsi E, Musetti S, Pasero M, Cámara F, Kampf AR, Škoda R, Mauro D, Zaccarini F, Castellaro F,清 Balestra C (2026) Belmonteite, CaMn2(AsO4)2(H2O)6·H2O, a new mineral with linear trimers of octahedra from the Cerille mine, Liguria, Italy. European Journal of Mineralogy 38:531-543

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Section 3 (p. 533) reports the calculated Gladstone-Dale compatibility index as 1 - (Kp/Kc) = -0.020 (superior), whereas direct evaluation from the reported nmean = 1.564, Dcalc = 2.662 g/cm3, and empirical composition yields 1 - (Kp/Kc) = +0.020 (opposite sign).

Section 5.1 (p. 535) reports R1 = 0.0226 for 1933 reflections with Fo > 4sigma(Fo), whereas Table 3 (p. 538) prints the header 'Fo > 4sigma(Fo)' as 1938 and the text in Section 5.1 lists 1938 as the total number of unique reflections.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Dacostaite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: Underground workings of the hydrothermal polymetallic deposit of Monte Arsiccio mine (Sant'Anna tectonic window, Southern Apuan Alps), Stazzema, Lucca Province, Tuscany, Italy
type_specimens: Holotype 20069 (Museo di Storia Naturale, Università di Pisa, Via Roma 79, Calci, Pisa, Italy)

primary_source.citation: Biagioni C, Bonaccorsi E, Musetti S, Sejkora J, Dolníček Z, Škoda R, Mauro D, Pagano R (2025) Dacostaite, K(Mg2Al)[Mg(H2O)6]2(AsO4)2F6·2H2O, a new thermodynamic-sink mineral from the Monte Arsiccio mine, Apuan Alps, Tuscany, Italy. European Journal of Mineralogy 37:39-52

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Section 3 (p. 40) reports the unit-cell volume refined from powder X-ray diffraction data (a = 12.2385(13), b = 13.6660(19), c = 7.2130(8) Å, beta = 94.716(12)°) as V = 1202.2(2) Å3, whereas direct evaluation V = a*b*c*sin(beta) from those four refined parameters yields 1202.31 Å3.
Table 2 (p. 44) lists the reference card for the strongest powder X-ray diffraction lines of metavoltine as 'PDF 20-0453', whereas page 42 (end of Section 3) cites 'PDF 29-0703'.

curated_sources_and_records.name: Fluormacraeite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: 2040 level (500 m above sea level) of the dump of the cubanite-bearing granite pegmatite mine at Hagendorf-Süd, near Waidhaus, Upper Palatinate (Oberpfalz), Bavaria, Germany
type_specimens: Holotype MM 44675 (Museums Victoria, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia; specimen number M56607 in Abstract)

primary_source.citation: Grey IE, Hochleitner R, Kampf AR, Boer S, MacRae CM, Cashion JD, Rewitzer C, Mumme WG (2025) Fluormacraeite, [(H2O)K]Mn2(Fe2Ti)(PO4)4(OF)(H2O)10·4H2O, the missing member of the paulkeitite group, from Hagendorf-Süd, Bavaria, Germany. European Journal of Mineralogy 37:169-179

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: The Abstract (p. 169) identifies the holotype specimen at Museums Victoria as 'M56607', whereas Section 2 (p. 170) reports the holotype registration number as 'MM 44675'.
Table 2 (p. 172) prints index hkl = '-2 2 1' for two consecutive reflections at dmeas = 4.544 Å (dcalc = 4.545 Å, I = 11) and dmeas = 4.499 Å (dcalc = 4.497 Å, I = 18).

curated_sources_and_records.name: Macraeite
curated_sources_and_records.type_locality: 67 m level of the granite pegmatite deposit at Hagendorf-Süd, near Waidhaus, Upper Palatinate (Oberpfalz), Bavaria, Germany; and Monte Rubio quarry, Castanheira de Pêra, Leiria District, Portugal (cotype locality)
type_specimens: Holotype M56293 (Museums Victoria, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia; specimen collected from the 67 m level of the Hagendorf-Süd mine, Bavaria, Germany)
Cotype M56294 (Museums Victoria, Melbourne, Victoria, Australia; specimen from the Monte Rubio quarry, Castanheira de Pêra, Leiria District, Portugal)

primary_source.citation: Grey IE, Hochleitner R, Rewitzer C, Kampf AR, MacRae CM, Gable RW, Mumme WG, Boer S, Davidson AL (2024) Macraeite, [(H2O)K]Mn2(Fe2Ti)(PO4)4[O(OH)](H2O)10·4H2O, a new monoclinic windhoekite-type mineral from the Hagendorf-Süd pegmatite, Bavaria, Germany. European Journal of Mineralogy 36:267-278

primary_source_discrepancies_documented: Section 3 (p. 269) reports the calculated density for the empirical formula with Z = 4 as 2.38 g/cm3 (and 2.39 g/cm3 for the ideal formula), whereas Table 3 (p. 273) lists Dcalc = 2.426 g/cm3 for the structural formula with Z = 4.

Table 1 (p. 269) prints the analytical total before the -O=F correction as 100.38 wt%, whereas the arithmetic sum of the 11 printed mean constituent values (K2O 4.52 + MnO 11.49 + CaO 0.13 + MgO 1.38 + ZnO 0.65 + Al2O3 0.59 + Fe2O3 15.86 + TiO2 7.51 + P2O5 29.55 + F 0.89 + H2O 27.80) is 100.37 wt% (giving 100.00 wt% after subtracting -O=F = 0.37 wt%, vs printed 100.01 wt%).
